description: Negation guard on the past-tense rewrite (audit commit ad3641395). replaceVerbAfterSubject (used by en-yesterday-irregular-beginner-past) carries a negative lookahead (?!\s+not\b) so a negated verb is NOT rewritten. When a past marker + (pronoun + target verb) are present but the verb is negated, the rule produces no change and the engine escalates to needs_ai rather than emitting a wrong fix (e.g. 'did not go'). Expectations encode the VERIFIED behaviour of correctWithTutorRules() on current main.
fp_risk_note: This rule's false-positive surface is negation: without the (?!\s+not\b) guard, 'Yesterday I do not go' would be mis-rewritten. The NEGATIVE cases here are the guard's core contract — negated past sentences (a recognized marker + 'pronoun + do/eat/have + not') must NOT fire the past rewrite; because the sentence is still detected as clearly-wrong but cannot be safely auto-fixed, the engine returns needs_ai (corrected=''). The POSITIVE cases are the non-negated counterparts that MUST still fire — proving the guard does not over-suppress ordinary past correction. A regression that loosens or drops the negation lookahead will turn these negatives into wrong rewrites.

positive.notes: Non-negated: rule fires normally (go -> went). Guard must not over-suppress.

positive.input: Last week I do my homework
positive.expectedCorrection: Last week I did my homework.

positive.input: Two days ago I eat rice
positive.expectedCorrection: Two days ago I ate rice.

negative.input: Yesterday I do not go to school
negative.notes: Guard core: 'do not' blocks the rewrite of 'do'; rule produces no change and the engine escalates to needs_ai instead of emitting a wrong fix.

negative.input: Last week I do not eat meat
negative.notes: Guard core: marker present + 'I do not'; guard blocks 'do', 'eat' isn't adjacent to a pronoun, so nothing fires -> needs_ai.

negative.input: Yesterday we do not have class
negative.notes: Guard core: 'we do not have' — guard blocks 'do'; no safe deterministic fix -> needs_ai.

negative.input: Yesterday she do not study for the test
negative.notes: Guard — different pronoun (she): past marker + 'she do not study'; guard blocks the rewrite, engine escalates to needs_ai.

negative.input: Last night he do not come home
negative.notes: Guard — different temporal marker ('last night') + third-person male pronoun: guard still blocks 'do not come' from being rewritten.

negative.input: Two days ago they do not finish the work
negative.notes: Guard — plural subject ('they') + marker 'two days ago': negation guard holds across plural pronouns.

negative.input: Yesterday I did not go to school
negative.expectedCorrection: Yesterday I did not go to school.
negative.notes: Already-correct past negation: 'did not go' is grammatically correct; the rule targets bare present verbs, so it does not match and the engine returns unchanged.

negative.input: Last week we do not see the movie
negative.notes: Guard — 'we do not see' with 'last week' marker: guard blocks 'see' from irregular-past rewrite -> needs_ai.

negative.input: Three days ago he do not eat breakfast
negative.notes: Guard — third-person male + 'three days ago' + 'eat': guard blocks 'do not eat' rewrite -> needs_ai. Distinct from ng-neg-001 (marker, pronoun, and verb all differ).
